ideas.hypothesis: Dynamic managed-lane tolls work as a screening menu that sorts drivers by their privately known value of time. Showing the travel-time savings explicitly sharpens the sorting, so more lane choices match drivers' stated value of time.
ideas.test: Toll transponder records linked to a stated-preference survey that elicits each driver's value of time. Compare how well lane choice matches value of time before and after signs showing travel-time savings are installed, against a corridor without the new signs.
ideas.disconfirming: Lane choice is no better aligned with value of time after the signs go up, or is unrelated to value of time in both periods.

ideas.hypothesis: Variable message signs that frame conditions as delay against normal travel time (a loss) divert more drivers than equivalent gain-framed messages. The effect is stronger for drivers who recently had delays.
ideas.test: A driving-simulator experiment, or a field A/B rotation of message framings on one sign, measuring diversion rates from loop detectors or simulator route choice.
ideas.disconfirming: Loss and gain framings produce the same diversion rates.

ideas.hypothesis: Face-to-face contact between corporate insiders and investment professionals raises informed trading in the firm's stock in the days that follow, visible as wider bid-ask spreads and a higher probability of informed trading.
ideas.test: Use investor-conference attendance and site-visit records as a proxy for colocation. Run an event study of daily spreads and PIN estimates in the five days after meetings versus matched non-meeting days.
ideas.disconfirming: Informed-trading measures do not change after colocation events.

ideas.hypothesis: First-time buyers using government equity-loan schemes pay a premium over comparable resale homes because developers have better information about values. The premium is larger where valuation uncertainty is higher.
ideas.test: Property transaction registry data on new-build sales with and without the scheme. Hedonic price regressions against nearby resales, interacted with local dispersion of valuations.
ideas.disconfirming: There is no scheme premium, or the premium does not vary with valuation uncertainty.

ideas.hypothesis: Commuters update their travel-time beliefs asymmetrically, as investors do in belief-persistence experiments. After a bad outcome on an alternative route, they discount real-time information that contradicts their habitual route.
ideas.test: Panel of navigation-app users. Model compliance with reroute suggestions as a function of whether the last deviation from the habitual route produced a gain or a loss in travel time.
ideas.disconfirming: Compliance responds symmetrically to past gains and losses.

ideas.hypothesis: Sharing real-time terminal queue and appointment information with drayage truckers reduces missed and late appointments, because it reduces hidden action between terminals and carriers.
ideas.test: Terminal appointment records before and after a freight traveler-information demonstration. Run difference-in-differences comparing participating and non-participating carriers on no-show and late-arrival rates.
ideas.disconfirming: No-show and late rates do not fall for participating carriers relative to controls.

ideas.hypothesis: In listed commercial banks, higher ownership concentration weakens the spread-reducing effect of periodic financial statement disclosure, because large blockholders already hold the information privately.
ideas.test: Daily bid-ask spreads for Jordanian commercial banks over several years, with ownership concentration from annual reports. Event study of spread changes around disclosure dates, interacted with concentration.
ideas.disconfirming: The disclosure-related change in spreads does not depend on ownership concentration.

ideas.hypothesis: Drivers who receive more useful crowdsourced incident reports go on to contribute more reports themselves. This reciprocity raises information quality on routes with dense user networks.
ideas.test: Navigation-app log data. Panel regression of each user's report contributions on prior exposure to other users' reports, using exogenous variation from incident timing.
ideas.disconfirming: Contributions are unrelated to prior receipt of crowdsourced reports.

ideas.hypothesis: Giving valuers GIS-derived accessibility measures, such as distance to transit stations, narrows the dispersion of their estimates for the same property.
ideas.test: Experiment with professional valuers who value identical property dossiers, randomized to receive or not receive GIS buffer-zone layers. Compare the coefficient of variation of estimates.
ideas.disconfirming: Dispersion is the same with and without GIS information.

ideas.hypothesis: Novice investors embedded in homophilous networks converge on similar information-accessing strategies and underperform novices with diverse ties.
ideas.test: Social-trading platform data with follower networks and trade histories. Measure network homophily, how similar users' information sources are, and risk-adjusted returns.
ideas.disconfirming: Homophily is unrelated to strategy similarity or to performance.

ideas.hypothesis: Borda-count rankings of traffic-information service attributes by users reproduce the priority order implied by structural equation model path coefficients on satisfaction, offering a cheaper way to set service priorities.
ideas.test: Survey of drivers that includes both a ranking task over service attributes and Likert satisfaction items. Compare the Borda order with the SEM coefficient order using Kendall's tau.
ideas.disconfirming: The two orderings agree only weakly (low tau).

ideas.hypothesis: Rollouts of advanced traveler information systems widen the gap in real-time travel information between higher- and lower-income travelers, because lower-income travelers rely more on radio, TV and roadside signs.
ideas.test: Household travel survey waves before and after a regional ATIS or app launch, recording information sources and unexpected delays by income group.
ideas.disconfirming: Information use and delay reductions show no income gradient.

ideas.hypothesis: The value of more accurate road-weather forecasts, measured as net savings in salting and plowing, is highest in districts whose temperatures often hover near freezing.
ideas.test: Maintenance district records of treatment actions and costs combined with historical forecast errors. Compute decision-theoretic value of information by district climate regime.
ideas.disconfirming: Value of information is uniform across climate regimes.

ideas.hypothesis: Once alternative digital data (web traffic, app usage, satellite imagery) begins to cover a firm, high-growth firms underinvest less, because outside investors are less uninformed about their growth opportunities.
ideas.test: Firm-level panel of investment, cash flow and market-to-book, with the start date of alternative-data coverage. Staggered difference-in-differences on investment-cash flow sensitivity.
ideas.disconfirming: Investment behavior of high-growth firms does not change after coverage begins.

ideas.hypothesis: Information asymmetry reduces dividend payouts more strongly for firms with greater growth opportunities, which prefer internal funds when outside equity is undervalued.
ideas.test: Panel of listed firms on one exchange. Regress payout ratio on bid-ask spread, market-to-book and their interaction, with firm controls.
ideas.disconfirming: The spread-payout relationship does not vary with growth opportunities.

ideas.hypothesis: Periodic financial disclosures reduce information asymmetry (spreads) more during economic crises than in calm periods, because uncertainty and adverse selection are higher then.
ideas.test: Event study of daily spreads around periodic disclosures for listed firms across crisis and non-crisis windows in one emerging market.
ideas.disconfirming: Disclosure-related spread reductions are the same or smaller during crises.

ideas.hypothesis: For startups offering new products in new markets, due diligence that weights soft information on founders' effectual reasoning predicts survival better than hard financial projections.
ideas.test: Code angel-group or accelerator deal memos for soft-information and financial-projection content. Link to three-year survival and compare predictive accuracy.
ideas.disconfirming: Soft-information content adds no predictive power beyond financial projections.

ideas.hypothesis: In markets with weaker enforcement, spreads widen and trading volume rises in the days before scheduled public disclosures, which indicates information leakage.
ideas.test: Daily spread and volume data around scheduled disclosure dates on two regional exchanges. Test for abnormal pre-announcement spreads and volume.
ideas.disconfirming: There are no abnormal pre-disclosure changes in spreads or volume.

ideas.hypothesis: Short training for new riders on how to use real-time arrival tools raises their transit trips in the following months, much as training novice investors in information-access strategies improves their performance.
ideas.test: Randomized trial among new fare-card holders, with a 15-minute training session versus none. Measure six-month ridership from smart-card taps.
ideas.disconfirming: Trained riders do not make more trips or stay riders longer than controls.

ideas.hypothesis: Real-time arrival displays at stops increase off-peak transit trips by older adults more than app-based real-time information does.
ideas.test: Staggered installation of stop displays, analyzed with smart-card data flagged by senior fare type, using difference-in-differences against stops without displays.
ideas.disconfirming: Senior ridership does not rise at stops with displays compared with stops without them.

ideas.hypothesis: Audible real-time arrival announcements at stops increase independent fixed-route transit trips by visually impaired riders and reduce their use of paratransit.
ideas.test: A small panel of registered visually impaired riders, before and after audio announcements are installed on selected routes. Compare fixed-route and paratransit trip counts.
ideas.disconfirming: Neither fixed-route nor paratransit use changes.

ideas.hypothesis: Spikes in gasoline prices raise consultation of real-time traffic information as drivers try to avoid fuel-wasting congestion.
ideas.test: Weekly time series of navigation-app or traffic-website sessions regressed on regional gasoline prices, controlling for season and traffic volume.
ideas.disconfirming: Information use is unrelated to gasoline prices.

ideas.hypothesis: Drivers who are overconfident about their route knowledge ignore managed-lane travel-time information more often, which leads to costlier lane choices.
ideas.test: Survey measuring how well drivers' confidence in travel-time estimates matches their actual travel times, linked to transponder lane-choice records and realized travel times.
ideas.disconfirming: Overconfidence is unrelated to whether choices follow the posted information.

ideas.hypothesis: Telling prospective first-time buyers about typical new-build premiums reduces their intention to use equity-loan schemes and shifts searches toward resale homes.
ideas.test: Randomized online information treatment among prospective buyers. Measure stated scheme intention and click-through to resale versus new-build listings.
ideas.disconfirming: The information treatment changes neither intentions nor search behavior.

ideas.hypothesis: Startups facing greater information asymmetry, such as those with new products in new markets, rely more on equity and convertible financing than on debt.
ideas.test: Startup survey panel data on financing sources, with a product and market novelty indicator. Fractional regression of the debt share.
ideas.disconfirming: The debt share is unrelated to novelty.

ideas.hypothesis: Visible privacy-preserving features, such as on-device processing and location coarsening, raise contribution rates to crowdsourced traffic data.
ideas.test: A/B test in a traffic app that randomizes a privacy-preserving data mode and its disclosure. Measure report contribution rates.
ideas.disconfirming: Contribution rates do not differ between arms.

ideas.hypothesis: Publishing automatic vehicle location data openly reduces rider complaints about reliability and perceived wait times even when actual service reliability is unchanged.
ideas.test: Agency complaint logs and rider satisfaction surveys before and after opening an AVL feed on some routes, controlling for on-time performance.
ideas.disconfirming: Complaints and perceived wait times do not change once actual reliability is controlled for.

ideas.hypothesis: Residents of dense, mixed-use neighborhoods consult pre-trip information less often, because nearby redundant options lower the cost of travel uncertainty.
ideas.test: Household travel survey with questions on information use, linked to neighborhood density and land-use mix. Regress information use on these, controlling for self-selection with attitude measures.
ideas.disconfirming: Pre-trip information use does not vary with urban form after controls.

ideas.hypothesis: A brief training module on managed-lane signs and entry rules improves correct entry decisions, as access-strategy training does for novice investors.
ideas.test: Driving-simulator randomized trial of trained versus untrained drivers, measuring correct entry and exit decisions on managed-lane scenarios.
ideas.disconfirming: Trained drivers make no more correct decisions than controls.

ideas.hypothesis: Routes whose real-time arrival predictions have larger errors lose ridership relative to routes with accurate predictions.
ideas.test: Route-month panel linking prediction error (predicted versus actual AVL arrivals) to boardings, with route and month fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Ridership is unrelated to prediction error.
